title: Pointers in C
misconceptions: A pointer variable stores the value of another variable directly instead of its memory address.
Dereferencing a pointer using the asterisk operator changes the memory address stored in the pointer.
Declaring a pointer automatically allocates memory for the data type it points to.
Pointer arithmetic increments the memory address by a fixed number of bytes regardless of the underlying data type size.
A NULL pointer points to memory address zero which can be safely read or written to like any other address.

rubric.text: Defines a pointer as a variable that stores a memory address.
Explains that the address-of operator retrieves the memory location of a variable.
Explains that dereferencing a pointer accesses the value located at the stored memory address.
States that uninitialized pointers contain garbage addresses rather than automatically allocated memory.
Explains that pointer arithmetic scales additions by the byte size of the pointed data type.
Defines a NULL pointer as a special value indicating that the pointer references no valid memory location.
Explains how pointers enable pass-by-reference behavior in function arguments to modify original variables.
